notes:
Summary: VeloxHound is a programmatic ad bidding platform that processes ~8k–12k RTB requests/sec during peak windows. Their main constraint is tail latency: auctions must be decided <30ms end-to-end P95, and they are highly cost sensitive on a per-request basis. They are evaluating Redwood for a Dedicated pool to replace a homegrown GPU-based runtime.

Customer goals and constraints:
- Target: P95 inference latency <= 25ms for a 256-token prompt (context + candidate features), steady-state throughput 10k qps with predictable autoscaling.
- Cost sensitivity: current infra cost baseline $0.30 per 1k requests; aim to reduce unit cost by >=20% while preserving quality.
- Model preferences: prefer quantized 7B/13B variants for reranker; willing to test mixed routing to smaller open models for low-criticality traffic.
- Reliability: need graceful fallback to a CPU-quantized model if GPU capacity temporarily unavailable.
- Compliance: SOC2 and SSO; encrypted at rest; want KMS integration for keys.

Technical asks from initial calls:
- Benchmarking: customer requested Redwood-run perf harness that simulates RTB fan-out: 1 central request -> 30 candidate reranks (batch + KV cache) with cold and warm cache runs. Keen on seeing P50/P95/P99 and token-level cost breakdown.
- Optimization interest: explicit ask for batching/caching guidance, suggested KV cache TTLs for repeated bidders, and quantization profile recommendations (8-bit vs 4-bit) with quality delta estimates.
- Integration: want a small-footprint SDK for their bidding microservices (Go + Rust) and a compatibility checklist for VPC peering and private endpoints.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "If we can't get sub-25ms P95 on our rerank path, we can't ship this integration." — CTO (R&D call 2026-02-27).
- "Cost per thousand is the single metric the finance team looks at; any improvement has to be measurable per-route." — Head of Ops.

POC plan (agreed in discovery):
- Week 0: security questionnaire + send staging keys (complete).
- Week 1: Redwood to run an initial perf sweep on hosted models (synthetic trace) and share CSV results.
- Week 2: Dedicated trial spin-up, 48-hour sustained run with customer's replayed auction trace (they will provide anonymized sample).
- Week 3: Joint quality check: compare top-N rerank decisions vs baseline; measure any precision/regression.
- Week 4: Cost model review and procurement draft.

Open items / blockers on our side:
- Need signed NDA to accept production trace for realistic perf runs.
- Security requires a short architectural diagram for Dedicated (they asked for network flow + KMS flow).
- Procurement needs clarified discount tiers for committed Dedicated capacity.

Asks for Redwood AE/SE team:
- SE: prepare a quantization A/B report (7B 8-bit vs 4-bit) showing inference latency, memory footprint, and top-N rerank recall for their evaluation set.
- AE: confirm Dedicated trial terms and include any accelerated onboarding credits; push procurement timeline to calendar.

Internal score: high technical fit. Risk: moderate (procurement/price negotiations). Next meeting scheduled: 2026-03-15 technical deep-dive (SE-led).
